parole.testo: Borrowed from Italian ciao (“hi”), from Venetan s-ciao, sciavo (“slave”) (in particular the expression s-ciao vostro, literally meaning "(I am) your slave" but in essence meaning "your humble servant"), from Medieval Latin sclavus (“slave”). Doublet of szláv. See also the similar etymology at szervu

parole.significato: to begin to understand; to get the hang of (something)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Italian capisco (first-person singular present of capire (“to understand”)) and Venetan capiso (first-person singular present of capir (“to understand”)), from Latin capiō (“to take in, understand”).
